newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Ultra-long range business jet paraded in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Ultra-long range business jet paraded in Hong Kong.

text.p: Gulfstream Aerospace Corp displayed the world's first ultra long range business jet in Hong Kong on Thursday, landing the jet at Kai Tak airport on the first Asian stop in an introductory world tour.
The Gulfstream V jet arrived in the territory from London in a flight that broke distance, speed and altitude records for business jet aircraft, the company said.

"It is the longest flight for a business jet ever from north London to Hong Kong," David Henderson, director of corporate communications at Gulfstream Aircraft Incorporated, a unit of manufacturers Gulfstream Aerospace Corp, told reporters.
The non-stop flight covered a distance of 5,170 nautical miles, the company said.
The jet hit a record speed of Mach 0.84 and a record altitude of 49,000 feet for the route, Henderson said.
The flying time was 12 hours three minutes, about an hour shorter than ordinary commercial flights, he said.
It was the second leg of the ultra long range jet's demonstration tour from Los Angeles, through London, Hong Kong, Beijing, and Tokyo, to New York.
The trips from Los Angeles to London and from Tokyo to New York also broke or would break records in speed and jet aircraft distance, the company said.
Henderson said the firm was tapping the growing Asian market for ultra long range business jets.
"Asian companies are doing so well that...the need for ultra long range business jets is more important now than ever."

Charles Williams, vice president, North Asia, at Gulfstream Aerospace's unit Gulfstream International Corp, noted Hong Kong's new Chek Lap Kok airport opening next year would provide a special facility for such aircraft although Kai Tak did not.
"They will have a place that they can stay where they can be maintained," he said. The facility would be available in the fourth quarter of 1998 after the airport's opening in April.
Gulfstream said its new plane boasts a range 50 percent greater than other business jets, and can carry eight passengers and a crew of four for non-stop distances up to 6,500 nautical miles.
Equipped with multi-channel telephones, fax machines and data satellite communications, the jet is designed to cruise at altitudes up to 51,000 feet.

Demand for the Gulfstream V jet has resulted in an order backlog that stretches into the first quarter of 2000, and the first completed planes will be delivered in June, the company said. Most customers were governments and private companies.
